analysis:
Integration of all 17 units: the PR removes leftover console-ui tooling and docs after the console source moved to darkbloom-platform (#1625). Changes cover the .githooks pre-commit/pre-push hooks, .github/dependabot.yml (npm /console-ui only), the lint-console job and its route entry in ci.yml, the console output in component-changes.yml, Makefile ui-* targets, two console-only coordinator test fixtures, the console architecture doc and screenshots, docs and config-reference edits, scripts/ci-component-paths.py, docs-impact-rules.json, merge-rules.json, and the matching test scripts. No provider runtime, TB-002 WebSocket handling, TB-009/TB-011 attestation and authorization, key custody, T-041 cache storage, TB-010 fan helper or TB-012 add-on socket code is touched. The replayed patches confirm this.

CI posture: ci.yml keeps top-level contents: read, SHA-pinned actions and the provider-test-gate. No new triggers, secrets or untrusted interpolation are added. test-ci-component-paths.py adds console-ui/ to the forbidden strings for public workflows, and the secrets/id-token/pull_request_target assertions remain. The merge-rules.json removal of the 'Console UI Lint & Build' required check is consistent with the removed job. It is a possible merge-blocking risk if the check were still required, not a security regression, and no bypass actors were added. Dependabot removal covers only a directory the changelog says no longer exists.

Residual unverified items, all outside the supplied evidence: the full ci-component-paths.py and test-script heads, whether any workflow still references needs.*.outputs.console (it would resolve empty, which is harmless), and the cross-repo claim that platform keeps byte-identical copies of the wire fixtures. These are documentation or CI-consistency matters. They are not evidence of a weakened provider security control, and no threat-model update is needed.
